fyNote: Financial year ends 31 December. 'Net income' is a bank's revenue: interest earned minus interest paid, plus fees and other income. 1H = January to June; 2026 unaudited. Next results: Q3 2026, due late November 2026.

sources.title: CIMB interim financial statements, half-year to 30 June 2026

segmentNote: A regional bank: Malaysia is home, with big operations in Indonesia (CIMB Niaga), Singapore and Thailand (AR p.73).

how.title: How CIMB makes money
how.text: Income = interest earned on loans - interest paid on deposits + fees, trading and Islamic banking income

items.tip: Wear and tear on buildings, computers and software.

items.tip: Corporate tax and zakat (Islamic levy) in each country.

Profit to shareholders

pnl.incomeNote: Net income is CIMB's revenue after paying interest on deposits. Plus RM0.73 per RM100 from joint ventures such as Touch 'n Go.

fiveYear.note: Full years; revenue here is net income. First half 2026: net income RM10.97bn (-1.2%), profit RM3.85bn (-0.2%), return on equity 11.0% (Q2 p.64).

rows.name: Consumer Banking
rows.tip: Home loans, car loans, cards, savings and wealth for individuals. 1H2026 profit before tax fell 16% on higher provisions (Q2 p.65).

rows.name: Wholesale Banking
rows.tip: Loans, bonds and treasury for large companies; 1H2026 profit before tax +7% (Q2 p.65).

rows.name: Commercial Banking
rows.tip: Loans and cash management for SMEs; 1H2026 profit before tax +12.6% (Q2 p.65).

rows.name: Digital assets and group funding
rows.tip: Treasury, digital banks and Touch 'n Go; 1H2026 profit before tax -16% (Q2 p.65).

segments.note: Full-year 2025 split (the interim report gives growth rates, not full segment figures). Malaysia earned 61% of 2025 profit before tax (AR p.72-73).

assets.label: Cash, interbank and central bank deposits

liabilities.label: Bank deposits, repos and bonds issued

balance.note: A bank's balance sheet is mostly other people's money: customer deposits fund the loans. Shareholders' funds are only about 9% of assets, which is why capital ratios matter.

safety.label: CET1 capital ratio
safety.plain: The bank's own capital as a cushion against losses, as a share of its risk-weighted loans.

safety.label: Gross impaired loans
safety.plain: Loans in trouble as a share of all loans. Lower is better.

safety.label: Loan loss allowance coverage (FY2025)
safety.plain: Money already set aside covers all of the troubled loans.

safety.label: Loan to deposit ratio (FY2025)
safety.plain: The bank lends out about RM86 of every RM100 deposited; the rest is kept liquid or invested.

safety.label: CASA ratio (FY2025)
safety.plain: Share of deposits in current and savings accounts, which pay little interest and keep funding cheap.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM76.4 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM10 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 incl. 7 sen special)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM6.7 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM65 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.1 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM11 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin 1H2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM35.13.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Net interest margin (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits: about RM2.13 a year on every RM100 lent. Management says it narrowed further in 1H2026 but expects the pressure to ease (Q2 p.64).

metrics.label: Cost to income (2Q2026)
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 of income, about RM45 is spent on staff, branches and IT, down 2 points from the previous quarter. Lower is more efficient.

metrics.label: CET1 capital ratio
metrics.plain: The bank's own capital as a cushion against losses, as a share of its risk-weighted loans.

metrics.label: Gross impaired loans
metrics.plain: Loans in trouble as a share of all loans. Lower is better.

metrics.label: Loan loss allowance coverage (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Money already set aside covers all of the troubled loans.

metrics.label: Loan to deposit ratio (FY2025)
metrics.plain: The bank lends out about RM86 of every RM100 deposited; the rest is kept liquid or invested.

metrics.label: CASA ratio (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Share of deposits in current and savings accounts, which pay little interest and keep funding cheap.

drivers.evidence: Net income fell 1.2% in 1H2026 as lower rates squeezed the net interest margin (Q2 p.64)
drivers.why: Lower rates shrink what the bank earns on each ringgit lent.

drivers.evidence: Management expects margin pressure to ease from loan repricing in Indonesia and cheaper deposits (Q2 p.64)
drivers.why: Would let interest income grow again.

drivers.evidence: Non-interest income up 6% quarter on quarter on wealth and treasury sales (Q2 p.64)
Loans +1.1% in the quarter (constant currency); a healthy loan pipeline (Q2 p.64; PR p.2)
drivers.why: More loans mean more interest income.

drivers.evidence: Gross impaired loans at an all-time low of 1.6% (Q2 p.64)
drivers.why: Fewer bad loans mean lower future losses.

drivers.evidence: Provisions rose 15.2% in 1H2026 on higher overlays (Q2 p.64)
drivers.why: Money set aside for possible losses lowers profit.

drivers.evidence: Operating expenses fell 1.2%; cost-to-income improved to 45.2% in 2Q2026 (Q2 p.64)
drivers.why: Efficiency protects profit while income is flat.

drivers.evidence: Consumer Banking profit before tax fell 16% in 1H2026 (Q2 p.65)
drivers.why: Its biggest income line is under pressure from margins and provisions.

drivers.evidence: Wholesale profit before tax +7% and Commercial +12.6% in 1H2026 (Q2 p.65)
drivers.why: Strong corporate and SME businesses offset consumer weakness.

drivers.evidence: TNG Group profit more than doubled in 1H2026; TNG Digital payment value +69% (PR p.2; Q2 p.65)
drivers.why: A fast-growing digital business shared with the bank.

drivers.evidence: Exited CIMB Thailand's auto finance business; moving capital to higher-return areas (PR p.2)
drivers.why: Short-term costs for better long-term returns.

drivers.evidence: 55% payout; up to RM2bn extra capital return by end-2027 (PR p.1; AR p.71)
About 9.7 times last-12-month profit and 1.1 times book value at RM7.08 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: Typical for a large Malaysian bank; re-rating needs higher ROE.

suppliers: Individuals and companies whose savings fund most of the loans: RM520bn of deposits and investment accounts
Investors and banks lending through bonds, sukuk, repos and interbank deposits
About 33,000 employees; personnel costs are RM3.1bn in 1H2026
IT systems, outsourced services, security and repairs
customers: Home, car and personal loans, cards, savings and wealth products
Corporate loans, bonds, deals advice and treasury
Touch 'n Go eWallet (a joint venture) and digital banks in the Philippines and Vietnam
supply.note: For a bank, depositors are effectively the suppliers of its money. The report does not name individual clients.

competitors.source: General market knowledge, not the report

competitors.how: Large banks competing with CIMB Niaga in Indonesia

competitors.name: Digital banks (GXBank and others)
competitors.how: New app-based banks competing for deposits

outlook.text: Regional demand across key markets remains relatively resilient; focus on asset and loan growth with a healthy pipeline (Q2 p.66; PR p.2).
Committed to the multi-year capital return plan, backed by a strong capital position (PR p.2).
Will optimise funding costs, cross-sell and keep costs disciplined under Forward30 (Q2 p.66).
Cautious on 2H2026: volatile energy prices, shifting trade policies, global conflicts and changing interest rates (Q2 p.66).

outlookOverall.text: Management keeps a cautious view of 2H2026 but says regional demand remains resilient (Q2 p.66).
